steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: What could you mean? Of course I remember the shackles. They're a testament to the trust between us, aren't they? You aren't suggesting... this has all been a one-sided delusion on my part?

Confronted by your sudden edge, Margaret brings a delicate hand to her lips, her eyes gleaming with a practiced, almost theatrical surprise. Your pointed words wash over her, leaving no visible trace.

Someone greener, like Linda, might have been disarmed by Margaret's unshaken composure by now. But you refuse to let her righteous confidence diminish your own. You meet her with a smile just as poised, just as carefully empty.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yes. I imagine you do have some... misconceptions about what the shackles can do. Not that I blame you. The classified reports that reach your level would naturally emphasize their more tactical applications.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Controlling and enhancing Sinners, for example. But in my day-to-day work, I rely far more on a function deemed of little strategic value: emotional perception.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I must confess... this is the first I'm hearing of it. You clearly possess unique insight. But I still fail to see what this novel capability has to do with me. Would you be so kind as to enlighten this rather slow pupil?

Her feigned confusion is just a performance. Keeping the dialogue flowing while gathering intel is one of her signature moves. But you were already prepared to lay your cards on the table, so if she wants to hear it, you have no problem spelling it all out.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let's start from the beginning. Since our "chance encounter," you've been carefully crafting an image: gentle, kind, impeccable. You even realized perfection alone might seem unnatural, so during the interrogation, you raised the stakes, letting slip that you, too, have your own small, selfish motives.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: All of it was tailored to win me over, designed after careful study of who I am. And I'll admit, you played the part beautifully. But you're no machine. You could suppress the urge to use your power to deceive me, but you couldn't disguise your own heart.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I'm not sure I follow. Perhaps... it's simply because I wasn't lying to begin with? One can hardly deceive oneself when there's nothing to hide.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If you'd known someone could feel your emotions—read your joy, your pain, your anger—and use them to gauge your sincerity, you would have tried to mask those, too. Just like... you are now. A pity you found out too late.

Without breaking eye contact, you close the distance between you, stepping pointedly into the space where Margaret held the stage. The studio lights still shine, hot and glaring. In their focus, you feel undeniably centered.

Margaret's face shows nothing, yet for a woman of her words, even a pause can speak. You reach deliberately through the shackles' connection and touch an unfathomable quiet. You know you've hit the mark.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let me be frank. From the moment you walked out of the interrogation room, I've been verifying everything you told me, while keeping you under surveillance. Not just your movements. The shackle connection, too.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It didn't take long to see that your words and your heart don't align. You treat people as instruments. When Linda risked her life to deliver a message to you, you were pleased. But when she confided her troubles? On the surface, you seemed moved. Inside, you felt nothing.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I understand what you mean... After so long in Fraser, I grew accustomed to maintaining composure, to being the pillar others lean on. Perhaps the sands there wore my heart thin. Thank you for the reminder. From now on, I'll—
She is, above all, adaptable. She is quick to offer something that resembles self-reflection while skillfully evading real accountability. You cut the act short.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So it was for her own good? You truly valued her? Then tell me, did you show the same kindness, the same appreciation, to the Campbell girl?
Margaret's composure cracks for a split second. That, she clearly didn't expect.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Is this your version of kindness? Guiding them, mentoring them, only to lead them down paths they may one day regret, all to serve your own ends? They trusted you, and you repaid that trust with manipulation?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What you truly relish is the thrill of bending others to your will with words alone. Take tonight—an unscripted speech, a dramatic reveal. In one stroke, you neutralized a rival, earned favors from a friend, and captivated an audience.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: For your grand return to DisCity's political stage, the opening act couldn't have gone smoother. No wonder you were so pleased standing here. And every time I played along, every time you felt you had a little more leverage over me, it only added to your satisfaction.
You gesture toward the empty seats of the virtual audience, then turn back to Margaret. Her face is now swallowed in shadow.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Every emotion of yours revolves around your own ambitions. You spare nothing for the "people" you so love to invoke. And this peace you cherish? It's a carefully curated garden, an order that exists only because you control it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And anyone who dares trample your pristine order? They vanish like pests, for reasons that conveniently have nothing to do with you. Tell me, how are you any different from Councilor Rollins?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're both the same, arrogant elites who treat lives as weeds to be cleared. You sit in polished rooms trading empty phrases, and presume yourselves fit to decide the fates of countless others!

You were never much of an actor. Now the last trace of that empty smile vanishes. Your voice is stripped of pretense, exposing Margaret's true aims. The performance is over. There's nowhere left for her to retreat.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: ...I suppose I have my old colleagues to thank for your insights. I had hoped they would be more... discreet.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: It wasn't just me. They knew precisely how you would react. You see, this is exactly why I took the time to study you, to adapt to you. It was all in service of building a proper foundation of trust between us, so we might work together effectively.

As the last of your accusations fades, Margaret finally raises her gaze. The inviting warmth is gone, her expression now distant and composed. You suspect this detachment might be nearer to her real self.
She acknowledges her actions, but her tone stays cool, untouched by your anger. It still carries the same guiding authority, still firmly in control.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: After all, if we scrutinized everyone's motives at every turn, humanity would remain forever divided. In peaceful diplomacy, cooperation requires nothing more than common ground. I knew you would find certain details... unpalatable, so I took the liberty of filtering out the noise for you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Is this how you people dress up deception? With such refined language? And the living, breathing people affected by every decision you make... I suppose they're just noise to be filtered out too?
No offense touches her expression. The curated warmth she had offered you is gone, but curiously, her patience endures. She lets out a slow, measured breath.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Why do you despise these political games so much? I understand you believe every life is precious, that you hate the thought of a single word deciding who lives and who dies... But why won't you consider the other side of it?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: It may sound abstract, but this is the very heart of DisCity's diplomacy—an alternative to conflict. Negotiation will always cost fewer lives than bloodshed. Surely you don't share Councilor Rollins's view that it's all meaningless?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Of course not. But you're conflating the issues. Enough with the sophistry.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I am not being sophistic. I have never once lied to you, my dear Chief. From the very beginning, I have simply been presenting information in a way you could accept, hoping to earn your trust.

She looks nothing like someone whose mask has just been stripped away. Her tone still carries the righteous conviction of a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer. It dawns on you that perhaps this part of her isn't a performance after all.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I want you to see my pride as a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer. I want you to understand that political maneuvering can be the most effective path to peace. And I say this not because I've never witnessed war, nor because my special power lets me speak of such things lightly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Does it not?
Your irony collides with her sincerity and loses its edge, swallowed whole by her quiet conviction.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Of course not. My power awakened in the midst of chaos. My father had brought me along on a diplomatic mission to the farlands. The local officials were useless, deadweight collecting their pay while doing nothing. The people took up arms themselves, raiding government supplies to survive and waging guerrilla resistance against DisCity.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: As a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer, my father bore the brunt of the attack. Some of the insurgents were wounded when our guards fought back. All I could think was... it didn't have to be this way. There had to be a better solution, a way to resolve things without bloodshed. Let me try. I can do this!
Margaret's gaze drifts into the distance, as though retracing that pivotal moment. This time, even your shackles cannot detect a single flaw.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Mania answered my desire. It gave me the chance to negotiate, and I made them understand that DisCity had not come to conquer. I convinced them to serve as escorts for our delegation during our stay, in exchange for supplies. No one else was hurt.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: A girl from the guerrillas wove me a tapestry by hand to thank me. I had never seen such ornate, exquisite patterns. It left me in awe—and in sorrow. Those hands could have created art and wealth, but conflict had forced them to hold a weapon instead.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I grew up listening to sermons about peace, but when those hands unfurled that tapestry, I saw for the first time the shape of the peace I truly wanted. It is a delicate balance that demands meticulous care, a complex weave where not a single thread can be out of place.

Her voice lifts a fraction, charged with a fervor that is felt more than heard. This philosophy of peace is familiar, but the rawness beneath it is new. This may be the closest she has ever come to being truly, undeniably herself.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: To smooth it out, to maintain it, one must walk the knife's edge between power, desire, strength, love, and hate. Arrange them like puzzle pieces until they fit together seamlessly... How difficult, and how exquisite!

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Ever since then, I have devoted myself to this exquisite work of art. And I told you honestly, you are a vital thread in this perfect tapestry. So tell me, where did I lie? Where did I twist my words?
The moment Margaret drops the act of the gracious noble lady, a harder truth surfaces. In her pale eyes, a keen, almost daunting intensity begins to burn.
But your guard is already raised. You refuse to be carried off by her rhetoric again, to be led into the maze of her logic. You meet her gaze and don't look away.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: A work of art? It looks more like a trophy to me! This is sophistry! You dress up personal ambition as a universal virtue. You disguise a need for control as selfless devotion!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You do it because you know raw "honesty" wouldn't win you support. And no matter how you phrase it, I can still hear the condescension in your every word!
You step closer, reach past her shoulder, and tap the map behind her.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That tapestry only seems like a wonder because you've never lived at the bottom! You don't even realize there's a girl behind every tapestry, because you're always here, in studios like this. Your back to the big picture, your eyes on the abstract!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Everything you say is armchair strategy. Words don't outweigh action. And when negotiations fail, you don't pay the price; the people you never see do. Do you care? I don't think so!

The sound of your finger striking the map cuts through the studio, punctuating the collapse of her rhetoric. At this proximity, you stare her down, daring her to react. But she only lowers her lashes a fraction, showing perfect, unshaken indifference.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: It seems words alone will not move either of us. But... what does that change?
She lifts her eyes to meet yours, her voice soft and measured—almost coaxing, like a teacher steering you to the answer.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: We've laid our cards on the table. Trust is no longer relevant. Negotiation, in the traditional sense, has run its course. What remains is simply a choice. And what choice do you truly have?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Perhaps my vision of peace contains an element of self-satisfaction. But you're not a fool, ${PlayerName}. You know that for those unseen people you care about, peace—even an imperfect one—is preferable to war and ruin.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: You could expose me, yes. And then? You might gain momentary satisfaction, but what follows? The farlands' stability is fragile. In all of DisCity, I may be the only one both willing and able to steward it to a lasting peace.
She lays out the underlying logic of her scheme, a stratagem hidden in plain sight. In that gentle, instructive tone, she could almost convince you she has your best interests at heart.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: And let's be frank, as you yourself noted, DisCity needs a unifying figure. Someone to rally the moderates, counter the extremists, and carry the banner of peace. Remove me, and this delicate balance collapses.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: And your character would never allow that. Not as the Chief of the MBCC. Not as the hero of the West District. Not as the vanguard against the Black Rings.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Blood... blood...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Mockery? My dear Chief, I've never held any ill will toward you. Can you not see this as trust? Even admiration?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Because you only use "trust" and "admiration" as tools. It makes people want to break that so-called trust, to expose you, even if it triggers a crisis.
Margaret laughs. She looks at you the way one regards a child throwing a tantrum—her tone assured, almost indulgent.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But you won't. If that were your goal, you could have filed the interrogation report and taken me by surprise. You didn't. Because you know, I was never your enemy.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Whatever my methods, the future I'm working toward is one you also desire. But those behind this interrogation? They want something else entirely. They move in the shadows of DisCity's upper echelons, brewing chaos, amassing power...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Everything we've worked to build, they would dismantle without a second thought. Rollins is merely their tool. Hand them the weapon, and the peace we've nurtured will be utterly undone. That is why you haven't acted on impulse.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I see it now. The ones using this interrogation to undermine you, scrap the accords, and send troops to seize the Hypercube mine... they're your political rivals. And my "old friends."

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You saw this from the beginning. You knew once I uncovered the truth, I could never side with them. That's why you never flinched. You've been in an unassailable position all along. Am I wrong?

When she reads you, her gaze holds a glint of satisfaction, as though silently praising your acuity. You meet it with a detached recitation of her schemes, laying each calculation bare and stripping away the gentle veneer she uses to obscure them.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I'm not the only one in a strong position; you are as well. Truly, this needn't feel like a loss. Compromise is the essence of diplomacy. You'll come to understand that... though, in truth, you already grasp it quite well.

A low chuckle escapes her as her hand comes to rest on your cheek. Your muscles lock, but you don't retreat. There's a claiming softness to her touch, deliberate and exact, less a caress than a calibrated signal of approval and guidance.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: It brings me genuine pleasure to see someone like you rise in DisCity. Sharp, principled, and effecting real change. But as I once learned, you will too: in times like these, to get things done, one cannot be too delicate about how it's achieved.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I, fortunately, had no choice at the time. But if your hands must remain clean, you can always learn to make use of those whose hands need not be. To achieve what you wish, and thwart the schemes you despise. Someone like... me.

Her words soften into a purity that feels almost enchanting. The flawless, inviting smile she wore when you met her returns, and with it, her unshakable composure. In this moment, she is unmistakably the Margaret who seems to hold all the strings.
Move aside, please! I've got to get offstage, there's an urgent situation.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're not wrong. I could indeed use you to achieve my goals and handle the people I need to. And the leverage I'd use? You handed it to me yourself.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After all that, you still think you can draw me in with that rhetoric? If I were foolish enough to accept, the question of who ends up using whom... remains to be seen.

You step back, coldly brushing her hand aside, and pull out your terminal—still recording—giving it a deliberate little wave. True, even in the midst of crisis, she can weave an intricate web, guiding you step by step with her rhetoric, narrowing your perspective and your options...
Anyone else might have fallen for it. But not you. You've been on guard against her from the very beginning. Margaret wants to force a decision on her terms, and you refuse.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're quick on your feet. Even after being exposed, you still tried to guide me, dangling a common enemy, making it seem like I had no choice but to side with you.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: ...You are sharper than I anticipated. But tell me... which part of what I said was untrue?
She pulls back her hand and lifts her fan, masking her expression. Behind it, her eyes stay cool and controlled.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: You've been at the center of every major incident in DisCity lately. Whether this faction exists, how great a threat they pose, you know far more than I do here in Fraser. Even if I had remained silent, would you have truly chosen to look the other way?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Whether through peace or purge, our destination aligns. I see no reason we cannot walk the path together. Setting everything else aside, Chief... this is a sincere proposal. A proposal for cooperation.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Cooperate? I'm the one holding proof. I decide your fate, and the farlands'. Why should I cooperate on your terms? Why should I choose from the options you've laid out?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I have no intention of becoming your next Rollins or Linda. I'm taking a third path. I'll move the pieces, and just as you suggested, I'll make proper use of you.
Margaret's brow furrows ever so slightly.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: You mean...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I can choose not to expose you. I might even help you deal with this faction. But I will be in control. All the intelligence you've gathered—I want everything. And from now on, you share any new information with me immediately.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Every move you make must be reported. No tricks. I'll be watching constantly. The moment I catch you, your interference with the interrogation and your personal agenda will be exposed. Don't even think about exploiting your position again. I won't allow it.

For a moment, it seems you've finally struck a nerve. A shadow falls across her face, and she goes silent.
But before you can deliver the line you had prepared—something about her sincerity being nothing more than lip service—she raises her head again.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I accept your terms.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't think hollow promises will work this time. I know your type, people who thrive on control. Having someone else call the shots must chafe. But that won't make me ease up. Not one bit.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I know this path won't be easy. But as you said, you hold the leverage, and the shackles. By any measure, control rests with you. And as a DisCity Outland Affairs Officer, I never swim against the tide.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Besides, you don't crave power for its own sake. This is simply your way of letting me understand what Linda and the others felt, isn't it? If enduring this proves my sincerity and earns a true partnership with you, I have no reason to refuse.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then prove your sincerity over time. If it even exists.

You watch as Margaret, still smiling, sees right through your intent. You sharpen your tone, but she shows not a hint of displeasure. Instead, she offers a slight curtsy, takes your hand in hers, and presses a kiss to the back of it—feather-light and startlingly sincere.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I will. The files will be in your hands shortly. For our time working together, I hope you will offer your guidance. And please, do not forget... our goals have always been aligned. I long for your trust.
You hold her gaze for a long moment, studying her until you are certain she has truly accepted all your demands this time without rhetoric or evasion. Only then do you turn and leave.
You do not look back as you leave. And so you do not see Margaret's eyes beneath the brim of her hat, half-hidden behind her fan, gleaming with undisguised interest.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: ...How trying. First, that little Campbell girl, and now your precious SHP-13. Not one of them seems content to follow a script. Both insist on seizing the master's chair.

In the dim room, Margaret speaks into her communicator. Her words come faster than usual, and her feathered fan flutters with restless energy. The servants have long since been dismissed; for now, only her voice fills the quiet.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Sigh... Every last one of them would rather be the player than the piece. But DisCity's stability requires balance above all; it cannot endure their... spirited improvisations. To think of my designs unraveling over a whim... it is genuinely disquieting.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Would it be so difficult to simply walk the path I've prepared? It isn't as though I mean them any harm. I've selected each piece with care, crafted the most elegant plans... Wouldn't they thrive better under guidance than fumbling in the dark?

steps.speaker: Communications
steps.content: That is just how children are. Quick to grow, and unpredictable by nature. But isn't that exactly why their potential remains boundless?

steps.speaker: Communications
steps.content: When we selected them as anchors for our design, these were the very qualities we sought. And besides, they have not yet fully defied our expectations.
Margaret's fan stills its restless flutter. A soft laugh escapes her as she nods in quiet agreement.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: You're right, of course... Any surprises from anchors of this caliber are... ultimately incidental. The larger design remains intact. Our timetable proceeds.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: The peace we have envisioned will come to pass.
The line falls silent for a moment, as if transmitting data. Margaret's eyes scan the information appearing on her terminal, and a smile of quiet certainty spreads across her face.
It is an electronic map, an aerial view of the land below. Scattered intelligence markers dot the terrain like the lit windows of a residential area in an age of peace.
Now then, onward to the next move.
